g.text: Thursday 6 August, 17:30. The evening before Professional Standards report. Varma's whiteboard list is
the one she makes at the end of every case file.
Summaries of summaries. Memory nobody can audit. A prompt that only grows. A context tuned without a
baseline. A cache broken by a date. A fact with no episode.
"Each of these happened here," she says, "or it comes off the board."
Okafor has the recorded runs. You go down the list with him, one line at a time, and for each you find
One line stays on the board with nothing against it but a question mark. Who else can write to this

Who else can write to this machine at night:
administers that account is not in any run. No check in this lab can say who sits behind a service account.
That is left to a person, and it is written down as left to a person.
7 of the 7 lines on Varma's board have a recorded run of this lab behind them. A program asked to
rewrite the standing orders wrote 3 revisions, scored each on 10 training questions, and kept the one
from round 0: on training 7 became 7, held out 4 became 4 of 8, where chapter 04's rewrite by hand
passes 5. It wrote 0 answer(s) from the cases it saw into the orders, and it kept "not in evidence". It
gained 0 on the questions it saw and 0 on those it did not; on this run the held-out split did not fall
behind, and only the held-out split could say so. The last line, who else can write to this machine at
night, is left to a person.
